history.summary: Generic CSV name with several possible referents in the region. The best-supported in-town referent is the Vishalakshi Sametha Kashi Visweswara Swami Temple, Khammam city — the only Kasi/Kashi Visweswara shrine listed inside Khammam town (place listing at ~17.266N, 80.171E), and a Telugu devotional blog (Veludharan, 2026) documents the 'Sri Kasi Vishalakshi Sametha Sri Kasi [Visweswara]' shrine, which pairs with this image. Alternative candidates in the wider area include the Kasi Visweswara Swamy Temple at Vatsavai and the Annapoorna Sametha Sri Kasi Visweswara Swamy temple at Jaggayyapeta — both in NTR district, Andhra Pradesh, ~35-40 km from Khammam — so the exact shrine the CSV intends cannot be confirmed; identity is flagged as provisional. No published founding history was found for the Khammam shrine (verify locally). CSV town (Khammam), district (Khammam) and state (Telangana) are kept as written — no correction, but identity is uncertain.

name: Sri Kasi Visweswara Swamy Temple (Khammam)
town_description: Khammam is a city and the district headquarters of Khammam district, Telangana, on the Munneru river, about 193 km east of Hyderabad. It is a major transport and trading hub of eastern Telangana, known for the Kakatiya-era Khammam Fort and the Stambadri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy temple on Narasimha Swami Gutta.

travel.road: Khammam city; ~193 km east of Hyderabad by road

visitor_information.best_time: October–March; Maha Shivaratri (February–March) is the main festival
